weatherEar: Cloudy with a chance of airdrop. Overnight lows near the 200-day average.

stories.headline: Printing Press Runs All Night, Prints Nothing But Confidence
stories.deck: Workers report the machine "just kept going"; economists call it the most bullish thing they have ever seen a roller do
stories.body:
The press ran all night. It ran hard and it ran true, and in the morning there was paper on the floor and the paper was good.

The foreman stood by the rollers. "She does not stop," he said. He did not say it twice. A man who says a thing twice does not believe it the first time.

Analysts gathered at the window at dawn. One of them had a chart. The chart went up and then it went sideways, and the analyst looked at it the way a man looks at the sea. **"Consolidation,"** he said, and the others nodded, because it is a good word and it costs nothing.

By six the ink was dry. By seven the first copies were gone. By eight a man in a hat asked whether any of this was real, and was told, gently, to read the stamp.

image.alt: The big printing press in the workshop, its rollers full of fresh paper

stories.headline: Local Furnace Declares Itself "Carbon Neutral" After Burning Only Things That Were Already On Fire
stories.deck: Environmental groups unsure how to feel
stories.body: The furnace, reached for comment between logs, said it had "never once started anything." Witnesses confirm the logs were, in every case, *already planning it*.

stories.headline: Man Who Said "It's Different This Time" Confirms It Was, In Fact, The Same
stories.body: And so it goes. He said it in 2017 and in 2021 and on Tuesday. On Wednesday he bought the top again, because he is a man of tradition.

stories.headline: PLANK HOLDER CHECKS PRICE 400 TIMES, PRICE DOES NOT NOTICE
stories.deck: "I thought if I looked at it enough it would look back," says devastated man
stories.body:
We were somewhere around the fourth refresh when the candles began to take hold. The chart was breathing. I remember saying something like *I feel a bit lightheaded, maybe you should drive.*

He did not drive. He refreshed. 401. 402. The number stayed exactly where it was, which is the cruelest thing a number can do to a man.

stories.headline: BREAKING: SOMEONE SOLD 3 PLANK
stories.deck: Community enters five stages of grief in under a minute
stories.body: Denial, anger, bargaining, a 40-reply thread and a new profile picture. Acceptance is scheduled for Thursday.

stories.headline: TANG GANG MEMBER "JUST HAS ONE ORANGE," HAS ELEVEN
stories.body:
She arrived at the party with one orange, which is charming, and left with eleven, which is a lifestyle. *"I can stop whenever I like,"* she said, peeling. "I simply don't like."

One does admire the commitment. One also admires a forest fire, from a distance.

stories.headline: NEW COIN PROMISES TO "FIX MONEY," LAUNCHES WITH 90% SUPPLY IN ONE WALLET
stories.deck: Founder: "That wallet is very trustworthy, it's mine"
stories.body: The whitepaper was one page long and the page was mostly a picture of a rocket. The roadmap said *Q1: Moon.* There was no Q2. Nobody asked about Q2. That is how you know it is a bull market.

image.alt: Bowling ball meme: me reading the whitepaper, page 1 of 1

stories.headline: GAS FEES DROP SO LOW MAN SENDS HIMSELF 0.0001 ETH JUST TO FEEL SOMETHING
stories.body: "It went through instantly," he said, staring into the middle distance. "I don't know what I expected."

stories.headline: NATION'S GROUP CHATS REACH 100% "LOL" BY VOLUME
stories.deck: Experts warn actual words could go extinct by spring
stories.body: A census of the nation's phones found that the average message now contains no information at all, which experts called "a return to form for human conversation."

captions: Scientists: we found a new species

stories.headline: INFLUENCER APOLOGIZES FOR APOLOGY
stories.deck: Third apology expected to apologize for the first two
stories.body: It was, as these things go, a beautiful apology: soft lighting, a grey hoodie, and not one word that meant anything.

stories.headline: MARKETS: THE NUMBERS DID THINGS
stories.deck: Real numbers, filled in by code. The jokes are ours.
stories.body: The market opened. It went down and then it went up and a man said he had known all along. He had not known. Nobody knows. That is the market.

stories.headline: OBITUARY: ONE (1) STOP-LOSS
stories.body: Once upon a midnight dreary, as the candles dipped so weary, rang a fill upon my ledger — *only this, and nothing more.* It sold the dip. The dip then rose. Quoth the chart: "Nevermore."
